description: CPU-first supercomputer at RIKEN, scheduled with Slurm, reached through shared front-end login nodes. Think CPU and MPI first.

login.auth: SSH key only (no passwords) — register your public key via the portal before first login
login.note: Login nodes are for editing, building, staging, and submitting only — anything heavier belongs in a job.
login.limits: Per user on a front-end node: 256 processes, 48 GiB virtual memory.

defaults.note: Set defaults.account (a project ID) in your user config file ~/.hpc-agent/hokusai.json; --account is mandatory.

account.policy: Every job is billed to a project with a finite core-time allowance under a fair-share policy; the balance recovers gradually and moves continuously — read it live with get_projects.

MPC.name: Massively Parallel Computer
MPC.role: the workhorse; most work runs here

LMC.name: Large Memory
LMC.role: jobs needing very large memory on a single host

partitions.name: mpc_l
partitions.note: The first 156 mpc nodes, not separate hardware.

partition_defaults.note: Billing is the maximum of the weighted resources (PriorityFlags=MAX_TRES): mpc/mpc_l max(cores, GiB); lmc max(cores, GiB/30); gpu/gpu_i max(cores, GiB/4, 28 x GPUs). Nodes are shared core by core between jobs. A job over a partition limit is accepted but never starts (EnforcePartLimits=NO; reason PartitionTimeLimit/PartitionNodeLimit). OverTimeLimit=30 minutes. Node counts and live occupancy change over time — read them with get_resources.

storage.use: larger datasets and shared project results
storage.note: Opt-in per project, requested through the portal and charged.
Separate Lustre file system, no user quota. Files deleted once unmodified for a week. Flat and world-writable: create /tmp_work/<user>. NOT mounted on the GPU nodes.

storage.use: fast per-job scratch for I/O-heavy stages
storage.note: TMPDIR=/tmp in jobs; ~105 GB on MPC, ~339 GB on GPU nodes; shared with other jobs on the node. Use a job-specific subdirectory and copy results out before the job ends.

software.primary_toolchain: Intel oneAPI — `module load intel` (default 25.3.0) brings the Intel compilers and Intel MPI together. 25.3.0 has only the LLVM compilers icx/icpx/ifx; the classic icc/icpc/ifort exist only under intel/23.02.1.

mpi.alternative: Open MPI (openmpi/4.1.6, with gcc/13.2.0) — its module CONFLICTS with Intel MPI; load one or the other (module purge before switching). Launch Open MPI binaries with `srun --mpi=pmix`.
mpi.launcher: srun — inherits the job's allocation, so you don't pass process counts. Slurm is 23.02, so srun does NOT inherit --cpus-per-task: threaded/hybrid jobs need `srun --cpus-per-task=<n>`. Intel MPI: plain srun (I_MPI_PMI_LIBRARY is set in jobs). Open MPI: srun --mpi=pmix. Never submit with --export=NONE (the job then cannot see the HOKUSAI module trees).

software.threads: Threaded code must be told its thread count (OMP_NUM_THREADS), matched to the cores reserved per process, or it runs far slower.
software.containers: Singularity — pull a public image or build your own; GPU container access is enabled automatically for GPU jobs
software.note: Confirm availability and versions live (module avail) — the catalogue evolves.

gpu.note: One GPU also reserves 28 CPU cores (14 per socket) and 112 GiB, and is billed as 28 cores. Max 4 GPUs (one node) per job. GPU is secondary on HBW2 and usually full — reach for it only when a workload genuinely needs one.

network.note: Compute nodes have no direct internet route; outbound connections are relayed through the front-end proxy on port 3128.

job_output.console_log: slurm-<jobid>.out, written in the directory the job was launched from
job_output.scheduling: Jobs are ordered by fair-share priority; a waiting job's reason comes from the scheduler (get_job_status).
